question: What is the main purpose of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: To isolate patients with chronic mental illness in large urban hospitals
options.B: To replace all primary health care clinics with specialized psychiatric wards
options.C: To promote social inclusion and equal opportunities for people with disabilities
options.D: To shift the financial cost of medical care entirely onto international donors

explanation: CBR focuses on empowering individuals with disabilities to access opportunities and live included lives within their own communities rather than in isolation. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h1)

question: How does CBR differ from traditional hospital-based psychiatric care?

options.A: CBR is managed only by foreign medical doctors
options.B: CBR delivers rehabilitation services directly within the local community setting
options.C: CBR completely prohibits the use of any pharmaceutical treatments
options.D: CBR relies exclusively on expensive imported medications

explanation: Traditional care keeps patients inside isolated facilities, whereas CBR takes services, support, and awareness right into the neighborhoods and villages where people reside. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h1)

question: The principle of sustainability in CBR mainly encourages the use of what?

options.A: Local resources and affordable community strategies
options.B: Strictly cash-only payments for every clinic visit
options.C: Exclusively high-tech equipment imported from abroad
options.D: Temporary foreign volunteers who leave after one month

explanation: Sustainability means programs can continue running using materials, people, and funds that are readily available within the local environment. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why is active participation of the patient and family considered a core CBR principle?

options.A: It prevents family members from asking questions about the diagnosis
options.B: It legally protects the hospital from being sued for malpractice
options.C: It ensures care plans respect personal preferences and foster self-reliance
options.D: It reduces the total number of working hours required by the nurse

explanation: When patients and families help make decisions, they feel valued, take ownership of the recovery process, and build lasting confidence. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is a primary clinical responsibility of a psychiatric nurse in a CBR program?

options.A: Ordering all medical supplies directly from international factories
options.B: Managing the financial budget of the national ministry of health
options.C: Constructing physical buildings for local primary health centers
options.D: Monitoring medication compliance and watching for signs of relapse

explanation: Nurses regularly check if clients are taking their drugs correctly and observe for early behavioral changes that indicate the illness might be returning. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h3)

question: A psychiatric nurse visits a client at home and notices early signs of a psychiatric relapse. What action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Advise the family to immediately lock the client inside a room until the mood passes
options.B: Review the current treatment plan, assess stressors, and collaborate with the multidisciplinary team
options.C: Wait for the client to come to the distant tertiary hospital next year
options.D: Discharge the client from the CBR program because treatment has failed

explanation: Early intervention involves assessing what triggered the relapse, adjusting support, and working with the team before full hospitalization becomes necessary. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h3)

question: Why is collaboration with traditional and religious leaders important in community mental health care?

options.A: They replace the need for professional nurses and social workers entirely
options.B: They provide the financial funding for all federal hospital budgets
options.C: They hold significant influence and can help mobilize the community against stigma
options.D: They are legally required to write official psychiatric prescriptions

explanation: Because many community members trust local and religious leaders, their involvement helps change negative attitudes and encourages families to seek help early. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the main reason a multidisciplinary team is essential in CBR?

options.A: Clients have diverse physical, psychological, social, and economic needs that one profession cannot cover alone
options.B: Government policies fine clinics that operate with only one nurse
options.C: Hospitals have too many idle workers who need field assignments
options.D: It stops professionals from arguing about who is in charge of the clinic

explanation: Recovery involves medical, social, and financial dimensions, requiring nurses, social workers, and trainers to combine their unique skills. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the main goal of vocational rehabilitation in mental health CBR?

options.A: To replace traditional school education for young children
options.B: To keep clients busy so they do not talk to their family members
options.C: To help clients learn practical skills for earning income and gaining independence
options.D: To train clients to become fully licensed medical doctors and nurses

explanation: Vocational training equips individuals with trades like farming or tailoring, enabling them to earn money and feel productive in society. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h5)

question: How does psychoeducation benefit families of clients with mental health conditions?

options.A: It legally transfers all medical responsibility away from the healthcare team
options.B: It empowers them with knowledge about the illness and how to handle crises effectively
options.C: It completely eliminates all stressful events from their household
options.D: It teaches them how to diagnose and prescribe psychiatric drugs independently

explanation: When families understand the condition and recognize early warning signs, they can provide supportive care and prevent emergency situations. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is a common misconception about mental illness that fuels community stigma?

options.A: Knowing that counseling and medication help recovery
options.B: Believing it is caused by curses, witchcraft, or personal moral failure
options.C: Understanding it as a treatable medical condition affecting brain chemistry
options.D: Recognizing that stress can trigger episodes in anyone

explanation: False beliefs attributing mental illness to supernatural curses or weakness often lead to harsh discrimination and delay proper medical treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h6)

question: A local market association refuses to allow a recovering psychiatric client to sell goods, claiming the person is dangerous. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?

options.A: Report the entire market union to the police for immediate arrest
options.B: Organize an educational session with market leaders to discuss mental health recovery and bust myths
options.C: Advise the client to move to a different town and never work again
options.D: Agree with the leaders because public safety always requires total isolation

explanation: Engaging community leaders directly with education helps correct false fears and promotes the social inclusion of recovering individuals. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge facing CBR implementation in Nigeria?

options.A: Widespread stigma and reliance on traditional healing homes
options.B: Severe shortage of trained mental health personnel at the primary care level
options.C: Excessive government funding and oversupply of psychiatric nurses in rural areas
options.D: Poor infrastructure and difficult rural road networks

explanation: Nigeria actually suffers from severe underfunding and a massive shortage of mental health professionals, making the first option completely false. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h7)

question: How can task-shifting help improve community-based mental health care in resource-limited settings?

options.A: By replacing all hospitals with commercial pharmacies
options.B: By stopping nurses from providing care so only doctors can work
options.C: By transferring all psychiatric patients out of the country for treatment
options.D: By training general community health workers to perform basic mental health tasks under supervision

explanation: Task-shifting expands the workforce by equipping local health staff to handle routine follow-ups and education, easing the burden on scarce specialists. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h7)
